evidence: BM 1973,0501.59-.62 are catalogued as same or very similar mould series.
BM EA90389, BM 1973,0501.28, and Louvre E20834 are catalogued as the same mould series.
BM Harpocrates harpist corpus has at least six similar mould variants and a production waster from Naukratis.
BM Priapus plaque family is described as using two very similar moulds at Naukratis.
serial_mould_production_at_naukratis.interpretation: Standardized serial production is real at whole-figurine level.

negative_mould_control.evidence: BM 1973,0501.35 and .37 are explicitly very similar but NOT from the same mould.
negative_mould_control.interpretation: Visual similarity alone is insufficient; curatorial mould diagnosis can reject a tempting match.

evidence: BM 1973,0501.23 is a separate hand-modelled insert phallus.
BM 1973,0501.45 had a separately made hollow two-piece moulded phallus inserted into a hole; stump survives.
BM 1973,0501.53 retains a socket after loss of the separately attached phallus.

best_dimensional_near_match.critical_caveat: BM records thickness while Louvre records width of a high-relief fragment. The axes may not be homologous. Direct calibrated 3D/orthographic measurements are required before treating this as a true shape match.

second_shape_cluster.interpretation: Both are slender standalone phallic objects, but ~13.2% ratio disagreement is too large for a common-template claim from public dimensions.

osiris_relic_signal.reason: No terracotta object in the current audited corpus has independent provenance identifying it as the physical phallus relic of Osiris.
